name: Public-evidence satellite maneuver benchmark
notes: Event labels are interval-censored public operator evidence. Verified-quiet controls require authoritative evidence that commanded orbital maneuvering was unavailable or the spacecraft had been passivated during the selected interval. Unknown windows are excluded from false-positive denominators.
data_attribution: Basic SSA orbital data from Space-Track.org, operated by U.S. Space Command. Public maneuver evidence is cited per case.
split_policy: All windows for a NORAD object belong to exactly one satellite-level split. The test objects were fixed before detector-v0.4 or physics-ML performance was evaluated on this version.

cases.description: NASA and SpaceX Dragon reboost demonstration.
ISS reboost using Progress 83P thrusters. The cited NASA source gives the date and duration but not a precise UTC start time.

Negative control after ERS-2 fuel depletion and complete passivation. ESA states its remaining fuel was burned off, batteries disconnected, transmitters switched off and the spacecraft could no longer be controlled.
Negative control after GIOVE-A decommissioning. ESA reports attitude/orbit control placed in standby, then the onboard computer and transmitter switched off.
Negative control after Meteosat-7 disposal. EUMETSAT reports the fuel tank was empty and the spacecraft instruments were switched off following graveyard-orbit disposal.
Sentinel-1A collision-avoidance maneuver during LEOP. ESA reports a 39-second maneuver executed at 05:14 UTC on 5 April 2014.
Negative control after GOCE's xenon fuel was depleted and its ion engine had been switched off. ESA describes the subsequent phase as natural orbital decay under atmospheric drag.
ESA reports 11 recovery maneuvers over 17 days; individual burn times are not public in the cited source.
Negative control after Meteosat-8 was moved to graveyard orbit. EUMETSAT reports residual propellant was depleted and all electrical equipment switched off.
INTEGRAL disposal-orbit campaign. ESA documents the largest burn on 24 January and another planned burn on 4 February; the case is interval-censored around the public burn schedule.
Unscored robustness window after the January reentry-targeting maneuvers. It remains unknown because later ESA reporting records an additional small trajectory adjustment before reentry.
